writeup: TIC 41831052 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 0.6826 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The system shows a primary eclipse with a depth of 0.03% dimming, yielding a detection significance of 14.7 in the Box Least Squares search. Pixel-level image analysis provides a difference-imaging peak signal-to-noise of 6.8, though the centroid offset of 11.9 arcsec from the target raises an important caveat: the margin between this star and a nearby bright neighbor is only 0.036 pixels, falling well within TESS's known centroid systematic uncertainty of 0.10-0.3 pixels. This means TESS cannot confidently separate the signal from the target star versus its nearby neighbor. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs. No secondary eclipse was detected.
